Abdul El-Sayed on Israel:
We have to separate between Judaism and the Jewish people and Israel and its actions. We have to. 
And I've tried to do that. People keep saying, "Well, because of your positions on Israel, you must also feel a certain way about Jewish people." 
I say, "Well, no, actually, we have to differentiate between our foreign policy."

Abdul El-Sayed on Israel:
You're still talking about apartheid policy in the West Bank. You're still talking about a genocide, but nobody wants to say that.
If I stand up and say, "Hey, maybe we shouldn't be sending our money to do the worst things to other people," people are like, "Well, it must be because you hate the people who are doing the worst things." 
I'm like, that's insane. It's actually insane.

Abdul El-Sayed on Israel:
I want to have a conversation where a Palestinian child and a Jewish-Israeli child growing up in the Holy Land can look forward at their life and say, "My life is not going to be curtailed by somebody's violence." 
How do we get there?

Abdul El-Sayed:
I know what it's like to drop off my kids at a mosque and wonder if they're going to be safe and whether I'm going to be able to pick them up safely afterwards. 
I think we are all united in the work of making sure that no matter who you are, you are safe in this country. 
And I'm committed to the safety of Jewish children like I'm committed to the safety of my own children.

Abdul El-Sayed on Trump:
I think people have always seen Donald Trump as this big monster that's unbeatable. 
It's funny what happens when you stand up to people and you beat them. 
Turns out you just stand up to him, and he can read the tea leaves.

Abdul El-Sayed:
I'm willing to work with anyone. I want to talk about something because I think people see our politics as this game where you get retribution on the other side. 
It's not about retribution. It should never be about retribution. It's about enforcing the rule of law and, most importantly, delivering for the American public.

Abdul El-Sayed:
I would rather a system where we're not helping a billionaire make a second billion, but instead helping a kid get a good education at a good school so maybe they can make their first million someday.
